precepts.text: Samuel's sons took bribes, so the elders asked for a king like all the nations, and it displeased Samuel. The Lord said, They have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them. The law was written knowing Israel would reject him; so he came down through David's loins to be king over them anyway.
precepts.point: When thou shalt say, I will set a king over me like as all the nations, thou shalt set him king whom the Lord shall choose, one from among thy brethren, not a stranger. The law allowed a king, chosen by God from our own people, which rules out voting.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 17:14-15 is law. If, when you get into your land, you decide you want a king like all the nations round about, the law says fine: set a king over you. But “whom the Lord thy God shall choose”: God has to choose him, you cannot. He must be “one from among thy brethren”, of your own people, and “thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother”: do not set a heathen over you. That scratches our voting right there.

Now 1 Samuel 8. “when Samuel was old, that he made his sons judges over Israel”, Joel and Abiah, judges in Beer-sheba. “And his sons walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes, and perverted judgment.” So the elders of Israel gathered to Samuel at Ramah and said, “now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.”

That is exactly what the law allowed. Samuel was righteous, and he was a priest, so it should not have been a problem. Yet “the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto the Lord.” Why would something found in the law upset such a righteous man? The Lord answers: “they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.”

That is why the law is there. The Lord knew Israel would want to be like the other nations, the Hamites, the Arabs, and would reject him ruling over them from the throne above. So he said: I have something for them. I will come down through David's loins and be king over them anyway, either up here or down there. We should not want a king over us; we have a king right there.

The Lord saw it before it happened. Israel was appointed, predestined, to desire a king over them and to reject him, and he came and ruled over them on the throne down here regardless. That goes to another level, a class in itself.

precepts.text: Thou shalt take no gift, for the gift blindeth the wise and perverteth the words of the righteous; that gift is what goes into bribes.
precepts.point: When Samuel was old he made his sons judges over Israel: Joel the firstborn and Abiah his second, judges in Beersheba. But his sons walked not in his ways; they turned aside after lucre, took bribes, and perverted judgment.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt take no gift: for the gift blindeth the wise, and perverteth the words of the righteous.” That gift is what goes into bribes.

Samuel's sons Joel and Abiah, judges in Beer-sheba, broke this very law: they “walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes, and perverted judgment.” The gift perverted their judgment just as the law said it would.

We see that same thing going on now in this political climate, and even in the church system. This is why the churches will not teach us who we are or teach the commandments of the Most High; when riots and unrest break out, it is those same pastors who go out to calm the people down.

precepts.text: If thou seest the oppression of the poor and violent perverting of judgment in a province, marvel not at the matter, for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; what Samuel's sons did is what we see today.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“If thou seest the oppression of the poor, and violent perverting of judgment and justice in a province, marvel not at the matter: for he that is higher than the highest regardeth; and there be higher than they.”

What Samuel's sons did, turning aside after lucre, taking bribes and perverting judgment, is what we see today. Do not marvel at it. The Most High, higher than the highest, regards it all.

precepts.text: Moses prophesied that Israel would come into the land and say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me; Moses was shown from the beginning to the end, he saw Israel rejecting the Lord, and he wrote it for us to read.
precepts.point: Where do we see that today? Voting. We are saying the same thing today when we vote, looking to a ruler like the nations instead of to the Most High.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
Moses prophesied this very moment: “When thou art come unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, and shalt possess it, and shalt dwell therein, and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me.”

And that is what the elders said at Ramah: “now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.” Your sons are not righteous like you, so instead of them judging us, give us a king like the other nations have. Moses was shown from the beginning to the end; he saw Israel rejecting the Lord, and he wrote it for us to read.

Where do we see that today? Voting. We are saying the same thing today when we vote, looking to a ruler like the nations instead of to the Most High.

precepts.text: The king was to be one whom the Lord thy God shall choose, one from among thy brethren; thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.
precepts.point: Where do we see that today? Voting. We are saying the same thing today when we vote, looking to a ruler like the nations instead of to the Most High.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
The law set the king: “Thou shalt in any wise set him king over thee, whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee: thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.”

Israel asked for a king “like all the nations”, not one whom the Lord would choose. When we rejected the Lord in our own land, that also set us up to be taken out of our own land and set in a land we did not know, under oppressors: strangers over us.

Now you hear people say, well, this one is the lesser of two evils; but they are both evil. We look at our condition now because this is what we sought: we rejected the Lord and said we want a king over us, we want to be like all the other nations.

precepts.text: Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem: your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time and served other gods, and the Most High took Abraham, multiplied his seed, and Jacob and his children went down into Egypt, where we served four hundred years.
precepts.point: Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“And Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem”: the elders, the heads, the judges and the officers, and “they presented themselves before God.”

Joshua rehearsed where we came from: “Your fathers dwelt on the other side of the flood in old time, even Terah, the father of Abraham, and the father of Nachor: and they served other gods.” The Most High took Abraham from there, “multiplied his seed, and gave him Isaac. And I gave unto Isaac Jacob and Esau”, and “Jacob and his children went down into Egypt”, where we served four hundred years.

Joshua warned us about the very thing Samuel faced. It was at Shechem that Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made. So the Lord told Samuel, “According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even unto this day, wherewith they have forsaken me, and served other gods, so do they also unto thee.”

precepts.text: Now therefore fear the Lord, and serve him in sincerity and in truth, and put away the gods which your fathers served; if you are sincere about serving the Lord, you are going to keep the commandments.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“Now therefore fear the Lord, and serve him in sincerity and in truth: and put away the gods which your fathers served on the other side of the flood, and in Egypt; and serve ye the Lord.”

How do we serve the Lord in sincerity and in truth? If you are sincere about serving the Lord, you are going to keep the commandments. A lot of people today say they love the Lord, yet they do not do any of his commandments; they do not truly show they have the faith of Christ, because they do not keep the commandments.

Israel at Samuel's time had done the opposite: they “have forsaken me, and served other gods.”

precepts.text: Choose you this day whom ye will serve; but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.
precepts.point: Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“choose you this day whom ye will serve … but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.”

A lot of us grew up with that plaque in the house, as for me and my house we will serve the Lord, and the house kept not one commandment: still eating pork, still keeping Sunday, still keeping the wicked pagan holidays of our oppressors.

Israel made its choice at Shechem. When they asked Samuel for a king, they were choosing again, and the Lord named it: “they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.”

precepts.text: The people answered, God forbid that we should forsake the Lord to serve other gods, for the Lord our God brought us up out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage; therefore will we also serve the Lord, for he is our God.
precepts.point: Joshua warned us about this. At Shechem, Israel made the covenant with its own mouth to serve the Lord and obey his voice; asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“And the people answered and said, God forbid that we should forsake the Lord, to serve other gods.” They gave the reason with their own mouths: “the Lord our God, he it is that brought us up and our fathers out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage, and which did those great signs in our sight.” “therefore will we also serve the Lord; for he is our God.”

That is the very deliverance the Lord pointed to when he spoke to Samuel: “since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even unto this day, wherewith they have forsaken me, and served other gods.” The people who said God forbid we should forsake him are the people who forsook him. Asking for a king was breaking the choice we ourselves made.

Joshua warned them what would follow: “If ye forsake the Lord, and serve strange gods, then he will turn and do you hurt, and consume you, after that he hath done you good.”

That is the warning Israel walked past when it asked for a king. The Lord had done them good, bringing them up out of Egypt, and they rejected him “that I should not reign over them.”

precepts.text: The people said, Nay, but we will serve the Lord; ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the Lord; the Lord our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey. We made that covenant.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“And the people said unto Joshua, Nay; but we will serve the Lord.” Joshua made them witnesses: “Ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the Lord, to serve him. And they said, We are witnesses.”

Then: “put away … the strange gods which are among you, and incline your heart unto the Lord God of Israel. And the people said unto Joshua, The Lord our God will we serve, and his voice will we obey.”

We made that covenant. So when the elders came to Samuel for a king, they were witnesses against themselves. The Lord told Samuel to “Hearken unto the voice of the people”, but they had sworn to obey his voice.

precepts.text: King Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel, thirty thousand men, and sent them to Lebanon ten thousand a month by courses: a month in Lebanon, two months at home.
precepts.point: The manner of the king came to pass under Solomon: he levied a tax, and the tax was men. Just as men go off to war, he sent them a month on and two months off to Lebanon, to prepare the timber and stones to build the house of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
The manner of the king came to pass under Solomon: “king Solomon raised a levy out of all Israel; and the levy was thirty thousand men.” He levied a tax, and the tax was men.

“And he sent them to Lebanon, ten thousand a month by courses: a month they were in Lebanon, and two months at home: and Adoniram was over the levy.” Just as men go off to war, he sent them a month on and two months off, to prepare the timber and stones to build the house of the Lord.

That is what Samuel told Israel: “He will take your sons, and appoint them for himself.”

precepts.text: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel were come out of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign, he began to build the house of the Lord.

“in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Israel were come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the month Zif, which is the second month … he began to build the house of the Lord.”

That building is what the levy of Israel's men was raised for: thirty thousand men sent to Lebanon by courses to prepare the timber and stones. The king Israel asked for took their sons for his work, just as Samuel said: they would “ear his ground”, “reap his harvest”, and “make his instruments of war.”

precepts.text: Of the children of Israel did Solomon make no bondmen, but they were men of war, his servants, his princes, his captains, and rulers of his chariots and his horsemen; five hundred and fifty chief officers bare rule over the people that wrought in the work.
precepts.point: The manner of the king came to pass under Solomon: he levied a tax, and the tax was men. Just as men go off to war, he sent them a month on and two months off to Lebanon, to prepare the timber and stones to build the house of the Lord.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

precepts.why:
“But of the children of Israel did Solomon make no bondmen: but they were men of war, and his servants, and his princes, and his captains, and rulers of his chariots, and his horsemen.”

That is word for word the manner of the king Samuel described: “He will take your sons, and appoint them for himself, for his chariots, and to be his horsemen”, “And he will appoint him captains over thousands, and captains over fifties.”

“These were the chief of the officers that were over Solomon’s work, five hundred and fifty, which bare rule over the people that wrought in the work.” The king's work, the king's captains, the king's chariots: “and ye shall be his servants.”

points: Nevertheless the people refused to obey the voice of Samuel; and they said, Nay, but we will have a king over us, that we also may be like all the nations, and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations

points: Samuel heard all the words of the people and rehearsed them in the ears of the Lord, and the Lord said, Hearken unto their voice, and make them a king; and Samuel sent every man unto his city.

note.label: 1 Samuel 8: Give Us a King Like All the Nations
